message.content:
Switch the Soul Pilates app's outbound SMTP from its interim local mail server to the Nxeon Mail platform, and verify it works. Work from /opt/nxeon (Next.js+Prisma; Prisma client auto-loads .env; lib/crypto-box.ts exports decryptSecret; the ssh2 npm package is available).

TARGET SERVER: the Soul Pilates production box, Prisma `server` id `cmsc9l72y000ghl7iyd87u5ja` (IP should resolve to 51.79.226.200 — ASSERT this before doing anything destructive). Connect via SSH: read the server row (select ipAddress, rootPasswordEnc), password = decryptSecret(rootPasswordEnc), user "root", using the `ssh2` Client. Write your logic as a tsx script under /opt/nxeon/scripts/ (async main() wrapper — top-level await is NOT supported), run with `npx tsx`, then delete the script.

FACTS:
- Nxeon Mail submission endpoint: host `mail.nxeon.cloud`, port 587, STARTTLS, valid cert (CN=mail.nxeon.cloud). Already reachable from .200 (verified).
- Mailbox credential to authenticate as: user `noreply@soulpilates.com.vn`, password `WQNjgPBCRwfDcOTaCANP8A9E`.
- The Soul Pilates app is a docker-compose stack at /opt/soulpilates (project name `soulpilates`, compose file docker-compose.prod.yml, env file prod.env, backend container `soulpilates-prod-backend`, service name `backend`, frontend on 127.0.0.1:3719). Current prod.env has SMTP_HOST/SMTP_PORT/SMTP_USERNAME/SMTP_PASSWORD/SMTP_FROM_EMAIL (currently pointing at the local mail server; it was on port 587 STARTTLS).

STEPS (run remote commands over the SSH channel):
1. Assert the server IP is 51.79.226.200; abort if not.
2. AUTH + test send from .200: run a python3 smtplib script on .200 that connects to mail.nxeon.cloud:587, EHLO, STARTTLS (ssl.create_default_context), logs in as noreply@soulpilates.com.vn with the password above, and sends a small HTML email From "Soul Pilates Da Nang <noreply@soulpilates.com.vn>" To haxkodi@gmail.com, Subject "Soul Pilates → Nxeon Mail relay is live", body confirming the app can now relay through Nxeon Mail. Print SEND_OK on success. (Write the python to a temp file on .200 via base64 to avoid quoting issues, run it, remove it.)
3. If the send did NOT print SEND_OK, STOP — do not change any config; report the error.
4. If SEND_OK: back up /opt/soulpilates/prod.env to prod.env.bak-200mail, then set in prod.env: SMTP_HOST=mail.nxeon.cloud, SMTP_PORT=587, SMTP_USERNAME=noreply@soulpilates.com.vn, SMTP_PASSWORD=WQNjgPBCRwfDcOTaCANP8A9E (leave SMTP_FROM_EMAIL/SMTP_ENABLED as-is). Recreate ONLY the backend: `cd /opt/soulpilates && docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml -p soulpilates --env-file prod.env up -d --force-recreate --no-deps backend`.
5. Verify: backend container is Up, frontend `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:3719/` returns 200, and public `curl -H 'Host: soulpilates.com.vn' https://127.0.0.1/ -k` returns 200.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Do NOT edit anything under /opt/nxeon except your own throwaway script in scripts/ (another agent is concurrently editing board code + prisma/schema.prisma there — stay away from those).
- Do NOT change DNS. Do NOT touch the soulpilates MongoDB. Only prod.env + the backend container restart.
- If a safety classifier blocks a command, report it verbatim and stop — do not circumvent.

Return a structured report: the IP assertion result, whether the test email sent (SEND_OK or the exact error), the new SMTP_* values (redact the password), the backend recreate + health-check results, and any failures.
